title: Quantitative 2: pacing
description: Twenty questions at the real pace of seventy two seconds each. Three of them, early in the set, are much slower than the rest, and that is deliberate. The skill being trained is noticing at about ninety seconds that a question is eating your time, flagging it, and moving on to the easier points behind it. One stubborn question can cost the five easy ones you never reach. On the SSAT a blank costs nothing, so only guess on a skipped question if you can rule out at least one choice. Come back to flagged questions if time is left.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is half of base times height: 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30. The choice 60 forgets to halve, which is the most common slip with triangles. The choice 16 adds the two numbers and 32 doubles that sum. Worth knowing cold: a triangle is half of the rectangle drawn around it.

questions.stem: Notebooks cost $3.75 each, or $13.00 for a pack of 4. What is the least it can cost to buy exactly 22 notebooks?
questions.explanation: This one was built to be slow. Five packs give 20 notebooks for $65.00, and two single notebooks add $7.50, for $72.50. Four packs and six singles cost $74.50, and buying all 22 singly costs $82.50. The choice $71.50 pays for five and a half packs, which the shop does not sell. If this took more than ninety seconds, the right move was to flag it and come back.

questions.stem: What is 4.8 ÷ 0.06?
questions.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 100 to clear the decimals: 480 ÷ 6 = 80. Dividing by a number smaller than 1 makes the result bigger than 4.8, which rules out 0.08 and 0.8 at a glance. The choice 8 moves the decimal point one place too few. A quick estimate before calculating catches this kind of slip.

questions.stem: After a 25% increase, the price of a jacket is $60. What was the price before the increase?
questions.explanation: The new price is 125% of the old one, so the old price is 60 ÷ 1.25 = 48. The choice $45 takes 25% of $60 off, but the 25% was taken of the original, smaller price. The choice $75 adds 25% instead of removing it. Check by going forwards: 25% of 48 is 12, and 48 + 12 = 60.

questions.stem: The average of six numbers is 15. One number is removed, and the average of the remaining five is 13. Then two new numbers, 17 and 30, are added. What is the average of the seven numbers now?
questions.explanation: This one was built to be slow. Work in totals, never in averages. Six numbers averaging 15 total 90. Five averaging 13 total 65. Adding 17 and 30 gives 112, and 112 ÷ 7 = 16. The choice 23.5 averages only the two new numbers, and 20 averages 13, 17 and 30 as if the 13 were a single number. If it took more than ninety seconds, flag it and move on.

questions.stem: Four consecutive whole numbers add up to 54. What is the smallest of them?
questions.explanation: The average of the four numbers is 54 ÷ 4 = 13.5, so they sit either side of it: 12, 13, 14 and 15. The smallest is 12. The choice 13.5 is the average, which is not even a whole number. The choices 13 and 14 are the middle two and 15 is the largest. Before answering, read the question again for which one it wants.

questions.stem: On a number line, what is the distance between -7 and 5?
questions.explanation: From -7 up to 0 is 7 units, and from 0 up to 5 is 5 more, so the distance is 12. A distance is never negative, which rules out -12 and -2. The choice 2 comes from 7 - 5, treating -7 as if it were 7. When one point is negative and the other positive, add their distances from zero.

questions.stem: A garden is shaped like a 12 m by 8 m rectangle with a 5 m by 3 m rectangle cut out of one corner. Fencing costs $4 per metre. How much does it cost to fence all the way around the garden?
questions.explanation: This one was built to be slow unless you know the shortcut. Cutting a rectangle out of a corner does not change the perimeter: the two outer edges you lose are replaced by two inner edges of exactly the same total length. So the fence is the same as for the full rectangle, 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m, and 40 × $4 = $160. The choice $324 uses the area, 81 square metres, instead of the perimeter. The choice $128 subtracts the cut edges and forgets to add the new ones.

questions.stem: What is 4% of 75?
questions.explanation: a% of b is always the same as b% of a, and 75% of 4 is easy: 3. Done the long way, 0.04 × 75 = 3. The choice 30 puts the decimal point in the wrong place, and 300 multiplies 4 by 75 without turning the percent into a decimal. Swapping the two numbers is a shortcut worth having on a timed test.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 42 square cm and a height of 7 cm. What is the length of its base?
questions.explanation: Area is half of base times height, so 42 = base × 7 ÷ 2. Double both sides to get 84 = base × 7, so the base is 12. The choice 6 divides 42 by 7 and forgets the half, which is the trap. Working back from an area is the same formula run in reverse; if the formula will not come, skip the question rather than sit on it.

questions.stem: Which of the following fractions is between 2/3 and 3/4?
questions.explanation: As decimals, 2/3 is about 0.667 and 3/4 is 0.75. The choices are 0.5, 0.6, 0.625, 0.65 and 0.7, so only 7/10 lands in the gap. The choice 13/20 is the near miss at 0.65, just below 2/3. Turning fractions into decimals, or into a common denominator, is faster and safer than comparing them by eye.

questions.stem: What is the value of 2 + 3² × 2?
questions.explanation: Exponents first: 3² is 9. Then multiply: 9 × 2 = 18. Then add: 2 + 18 = 20. The choice 22 adds 2 + 9 before multiplying. The choice 50 adds 2 + 3 before squaring. The order of operations decides the whole answer, and each wrong choice is an order a rushed reader might use.

questions.stem: The average of five numbers is 20. When one of the numbers is removed, the average of the other four is 18. What number was removed?
questions.explanation: Five numbers averaging 20 total 100. Four averaging 18 total 72. The removed number is 100 - 72 = 28. The choice 2 is the difference between the two averages, which is not the same as the difference between the totals. Turn every average into a total before doing anything else.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 54 cm. How long is each side?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has six equal sides, so each is 54 ÷ 6 = 9 cm. The choice 6.75 divides by 8, which is an octagon, and 5.4 divides by 10. Count the sides from the name: hex means six.

questions.stem: In a club of 35 members, the ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 5. How many girls are in the club?
questions.explanation: A ratio of 2 : 5 means 7 equal parts. Each part is 35 ÷ 7 = 5 members, so there are 5 × 5 = 25 girls. The choice 10 is the number of boys. The choice 14 is two fifths of 35, which forgets that the club is split into seven parts, not five. Add the numbers in the ratio first.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 3 times as long as it is wide, and its perimeter is 48 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: If the width is w, the length is 3w and the perimeter is w + 3w + w + 3w = 8w. So 8w = 48 and w = 6, making the length 18 and the area 6 × 18 = 108. The choice 144 treats the shape as a square with side 12. The choice 432 uses 48 as the length plus the width instead of the whole perimeter. A quick sketch with all four sides labelled prevents both.

questions.stem: What is the value of (-4) × 3 - (-5)?
questions.explanation: (-4) × 3 is -12. Subtracting -5 is the same as adding 5, so -12 + 5 = -7. The choice -17 subtracts 5 instead of adding it, the classic sign slip. The choice 7 drops the negative from -12. Rewrite every minus a negative as plus before you calculate.

questions.stem: Ana spent 1/3 of her money on a book and then 1/2 of what was left on lunch. She has $20 left. How much did she have at the start?
questions.explanation: After the book, 2/3 of her money is left. Spending half of that leaves 1/3 of the original, and that third is $20, so she started with $60. The choice $40 undoes only the lunch, and $30 undoes only the book. Check forwards: a third of 60 is 20, leaving 40; half of 40 is 20, leaving 20.

questions.stem: What is the median of 8, 3, 12, 5, 10 and 6?
questions.explanation: In order the numbers are 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12. With six numbers there are two in the middle, 6 and 8, and the median is halfway between them: 7. The choice 7 1/3 is the mean, 44 ÷ 6. The choice 9 is the range, 12 - 3. Sort the list first, every time.

questions.stem: How many centimetres are in 2.4 metres?
questions.explanation: There are 100 centimetres in a metre, so 2.4 m is 2.4 × 100 = 240 cm. The choice 24 multiplies by 10 instead of 100, and the smaller choices divide instead of multiplying. Converting to a smaller unit always gives a bigger number.
